guideTitle: 6 Best Splatter Screens for Cast Iron in 2026
metaTitle: 6 Best Splatter Screens for Cast Iron (2026)
metaDescription: Six stainless splatter screens for cast iron skillets compared by diameter, heat rating, handle and cleanup, for searing steaks, chops and bacon.
introParagraphs: Cast iron is the pan people reach for when they want a hard sear, and a hard sear is exactly when a skillet throws the most fat. A steak laid into a ripping hot 12 inch pan spits droplets over the rim, onto the stove and across the front of your shirt, and a pan this heavy is awkward to move once the mess has started. A splatter screen over the top keeps that spray in the pan while letting steam leave, so the crust you are building keeps its edge.

Cast iron has quirks that change what you should look for. The pans run wider than many nonstick skillets, with 12 and even 14 inch diameters common, so a standard 11 inch screen may fall short. The rim sits over a very hot surface for a long time, so a screen material and handle that tolerate heat matter. This guide compares six stainless screens: the BergKoch 15 inch, the FOXEL 14 inch, the ALPHA LIVING 13 inch, the U.S. Kitchen Supply 13 inch and 4-piece set, and the KORCCI 11 inch.

We evaluated each model from its listing, stated dimensions and materials, and recurring buyer comments, without claiming hands-on testing. The comparison looks at diameter against your skillet, heat tolerance of the handle, how the screen rests when lifted, and how easy it is to clean the fat that gets caught in the mesh.

products.name: BergKoch 15 Inch Stainless Splatter Screen
products.description:
Large cast iron is where small screens fail, and the BergKoch 15 inch is the model that clears even a wide pan. The listing gives a 15 inch diameter, 304 grade stainless steel and an extra fine mesh, and it describes the size as universal enough to fit all cookware. For a 12 inch skillet that leaves a comfortable overhang, and for a 14 inch skillet it is the only screen here with real margin.

The resting feet are a practical bonus with cast iron. After a sear you often lift the screen aside to turn the meat, and an upside-down mesh disc can leave grease on the counter. The feet hold the greasy face above the surface so you can set it on a trivet or counter while you plate. The listing also says the mesh is easy to clean, though fat that has been seared on is easier to remove with a soak.

Its size is the drawback. It is bulky in a cabinet and awkward on a small pan. Compared with the FOXEL 14 inch, it is a bit wider but lacks a folding handle. If your skillet is 12 inches or larger and you sear often, this is the best fit.
products.bestFor: 12 to 14 inch cast iron skillets and Dutch-oven-style pans.
pros: Resting feet keep grease off the counter
Plenty of overhang for sear spray

products.name: FOXEL 14 Inch Dishwasher-Safe Splatter Screen
products.description:
The FOXEL splatter screen measures 14 inches and builds on a stainless steel outer ring with a micro-mesh center. The feature that sets it apart is the folding heat-resistant silicone handle, which the listing says helps the screen slide into a dishwasher, unlike many screens with long fixed handles. For a heavy cast iron cook who already washes a lot of cookware, that convenience adds up.

A 14 inch screen is a smart match for the 12 inch skillet, the pan size cast iron brands sell most, and it still works for 10 inch pans with room to spare. The micro-mesh lets steam through while blocking spray, and the silicone on the handle keeps your grip away from the metal near the heat. The listing is playful in tone, but the facts are the ring, the mesh, the folding handle and dishwasher fit.

It does not come with resting feet, so you will need a clean surface when you set it aside. Compared with the BergKoch, it is a size smaller and trades feet for a folding handle and machine washing. If you want a large screen that goes in the dishwasher and stores more neatly, it is a strong pick.
products.bestFor: 12 inch cast iron skillets and cooks who want a dishwasher-friendly screen.
pros: 14 inch size fits 12 inch skillets with margin
Fits in the dishwasher per the listing
cons: Silicone handle needs care near flame

products.name: ALPHA LIVING 13 Inch Splatter Guard and Food Strainer
products.description:
The ALPHA LIVING screen is useful for cast iron mainly because it gives a number: the listing says the stainless steel splatter guard handles up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. Cast iron cooks hot, and searing temperatures climb quickly, so a stated limit is more reassuring than vague talk about heat resistance. It is a 13 inch screen that the maker says also works as a food strainer.

The strainer role is a genuine second job. After boiling pasta or rinsing vegetables, a fine stainless mesh doubles as a quick colander for smaller portions, which suits a kitchen that does not want another single-use tool. The listing says the guard is dishwasher safe and easy to wipe, so it can go through the dishwasher with your skillet.

A 13 inch screen is just enough for a 12 inch skillet and slightly tight on a 12 inch pan with a pour spout, so check that the spout does not leave a gap. Compared with the FOXEL, it is smaller and has no folding handle. Compared with the U.S. Kitchen Supply 13 inch, it adds the temperature number and the strainer use. It is the most informative pick on heat.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a stated 450 degree rating and a screen that doubles as a strainer.
pros: Listing states heat resistance up to 450 F
cons: Tight on skillets with wide spouts

products.name: U.S. Kitchen Supply 13 Inch Fine Mesh Splatter Guard
products.description:
The U.S. Kitchen Supply 13 inch screen is the plain, dependable choice. The listing describes a stainless steel splash guard with fine mesh that stops grease and oil splatters while letting steam escape, a comfortable grip handle, and built-in resting feet that keep the screen from lying flat on the countertop. For cast iron, those feet and the fine mesh are exactly what you want.

Most seared foods give off a lot of steam in the first minute, so a mesh that vents well keeps the surface drier and helps the crust form. The grip handle gives you a way to lift the screen without touching the rim, which is useful because the screen itself will warm over a hot pan. The maker also positions it for pots and pans in general, so it works beyond skillets.

At 13 inches it matches the BergKoch 13 inch idea but costs you the extra width of the 15 inch. Compared with the ALPHA LIVING, it has feet but no stated heat rating. Compared with the 4-piece set from the same maker, it is a single screen for one pan. If you want a solid screen with no fuss, it is hard to fault.
products.bestFor: A single 12 inch cast iron skillet used for searing and frying.
pros: Fine mesh vents steam while blocking grease
Works on pots as well as skillets

products.name: U.S. Kitchen Supply 4-Piece Splatter Guard Set
products.description:
A cast iron collection often has several sizes: a small 8 inch skillet for eggs, a 10 inch workhorse, a 12 inch for family meals, and sometimes a grill pan. The U.S. Kitchen Supply 4-piece set matches that spread with 13, 11.5, 10 and 8 inch screens, all in fine stainless mesh with grip handles. The listing describes the mesh as made to block oil and grease while letting steam escape.

Having a screen per pan means you never improvise with one that is too small. The 13 inch covers a 12 inch skillet, the 11.5 inch suits a 10 or 11 inch pan, and the smaller ones handle egg pans and saucepans. The listing also notes the handle attachment helps hold oil back, which is a detail that matters when a screen is lifted often.

The cost is storage, since four screens take room. Compared with the single 13 inch from the same maker, you pay in space for versatility. Compared with the BergKoch 15 inch, the set has no larger option for oversized pans. If you own multiple skillets, it is the best match.
products.bestFor: Owners of several cast iron skillets from 8 to 12 inches.
pros: Handle attachment designed to hold oil back

products.name: KORCCI 11 Inch Stainless Fine Mesh Splatter Screen
products.description:
The KORCCI is the compact option, an 11 inch screen in polished stainless steel with an evenly spaced fine twill mesh. The listing says the metal resists acid and corrosion and has good thermal stability, and that the mesh blocks hot oil and water to protect your eyes and hands. It is meant for a variety of household pots and pans.

For cast iron this size fits the classic 10 inch skillet well and works on an 8 inch pan with ease. It is not the right choice for a 12 inch skillet, where an 11 inch screen leaves the rim partly uncovered. The twill mesh lets steam through while holding back spray, which suits quick pan-fried foods like cutlets, bacon and burgers.

Because the listing does not mention feet, a folding handle or a stated heat rating, check the product page for those details. Compared with the U.S. Kitchen Supply 4-piece set it is a single smaller screen. Compared with the BergKoch it is easier to store. If your daily pan is a 10 inch skillet, it covers it without excess bulk.
products.bestFor: 10 inch cast iron skillets and small pans.
pros: Fine twill mesh blocks hot oil
cons: Feet and handle details are limited

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cast iron skillets are sold by diameter at the rim, commonly 8, 10, 12 and 14 inches, and the screen must cover the whole opening. A screen at least as wide as the rim stops the sideways spray that makes the biggest mess. The BergKoch is 15 inches, the FOXEL is 14, the ALPHA LIVING and U.S. Kitchen Supply are 13 and the KORCCI is 11. A 12 inch skillet needs at least the 13 inch size.

Searing in cast iron brings the pan well above ordinary frying temperatures, and the screen and handle sit just above it. The ALPHA LIVING listing states resistance up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit, which is useful information. Handles that are plain stainless can get hot, while silicone-covered handles such as the FOXEL's stay more comfortable. Check the maker's limit before using a screen on a very hot pan.

A good sear depends on steam leaving the pan so the surface stays dry. Fine stainless mesh, like the U.S. Kitchen Supply, KORCCI and BergKoch designs, blocks droplets and lets vapor through. A screen with holes that are too small or clogged can trap steam, so keep it clean. Lift it briefly when you flip to release trapped moisture.

With a heavy pan you are often managing the skillet in one hand and the screen in the other. A comfortable grip handle, a folding handle as on the FOXEL, or resting feet as on the BergKoch and U.S. Kitchen Supply make that easier. Feet keep greasy mesh off the counter, which saves cleanup. Think about where you will put the screen while you plate.

High heat bakes fat into mesh, and unlike a flat pan the screen cannot be scrubbed with a wire pad without damaging it. Soak in hot water with dish soap, or add a spoon of baking soda, then use a soft brush. The FOXEL and ALPHA LIVING are listed as dishwasher safe, which helps. Clean the screen the same day for best results.

If you own one cast iron skillet, a single screen like the U.S. Kitchen Supply 13 inch or the FOXEL is enough. If you own several sizes, the 4-piece set covers 8 to 13 inches. Consider your storage too: four screens need a hook or a deep drawer. Buy the set only if you will use more than two sizes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Diameter versus skillet size
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated diameters against the 8, 10, 12 and 14 inch skillets common in cast iron. The BergKoch 15 inch and FOXEL 14 inch lead on coverage, and the KORCCI 11 inch is the smallest. Models that fit the largest pans earned more credit for cast iron.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat information
howWeEvaluated.description: Cast iron cooks hot, so we looked for stated temperature limits and handle materials. The ALPHA LIVING lists 450 degrees Fahrenheit, and the FOXEL uses a heat-resistant silicone handle. Listings with no heat information were scored cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mesh and venting
howWeEvaluated.description: Fine stainless mesh was compared across the group for how it blocks spray while releasing steam. The U.S. Kitchen Supply, KORCCI and BergKoch designs all use fine mesh. We relied on listings and buyer comments about clogging.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: Resting feet, folding handles and set sizes were weighed. The BergKoch and U.S. Kitchen Supply 13 inch have feet, and the FOXEL folds its handle. The 4-piece set offers coverage but needs more storage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: Within this group, the BergKoch leads on size, the FOXEL on storage and dishwasher fit, the ALPHA LIVING on heat data, the U.S. Kitchen Supply 13 inch on simplicity, the 4-piece set on variety and the KORCCI on compactness.

faq.q: What size splatter screen fits a 12 inch cast iron skillet?
faq.a: A 13 inch screen covers the rim of a standard 12 inch skillet, as with the ALPHA LIVING and U.S. Kitchen Supply 13 inch models. If your skillet has pour spouts, a 14 inch screen like the FOXEL gives more margin. Measure the rim, not the cooking surface.

faq.q: Is it safe to use a screen when searing at high heat?
faq.a: Stainless screens generally handle sear temperatures, and the ALPHA LIVING lists resistance up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. Handles can get hot, so use a screen with a grip or silicone handle and hold it away from the flame. Check the listed limit before using it on a very hot pan.

faq.q: Will a screen stop my steak from searing?
faq.a: A fine mesh lets steam escape, so it does not prevent a crust the way a lid would. You can lift the screen briefly or remove it for the last minute. Keep the mesh clean so it does not clog.

faq.q: How do I clean a screen after cast iron cooking?
faq.a: Soak it in hot water with dish soap, and add baking soda for stubborn fat. Scrub gently with a soft brush. The FOXEL and ALPHA LIVING are listed as dishwasher safe, which makes cleanup quicker.

faq.q: Do I need a screen if I already season my pan well?
faq.a: Seasoning does not stop oil from spitting when moisture hits hot fat. A screen controls the spray regardless of seasoning. It keeps your stove and sleeves cleaner while you cook.

faq.q: Can I use a screen on a Dutch oven or grill pan?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the diameter covers the rim. The BergKoch 15 inch fits wide Dutch ovens, and the U.S. Kitchen Supply set covers smaller pots. Grill pans with ridges throw spray upward, so a wide screen helps.
